items.hook: World War II: Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union sign the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact. In a secret protocol to the pact, Poland, Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Romania are divided into German and Soviet "spheres of influence".
items.body: World War II, or the Second World War, was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Axis powers. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: World War II: King Michael of Romania dismisses the pro-Nazi government of Marshal Antonescu, who is later arrested. Romania switches sides from the Axis to the Allies.
items.body: Michael I was the last king of Romania, reigning from 20 July 1927 to 8 June 1930 and again from 6 September 1940 until his forced abdication on 30 December 1947. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The USCGC Acacia (WAGL-406/WLB-406) is an Iris-class 180-foot seagoing buoy tender operated by the United States Coast Guard.
items.body: Acacia was a multi-purpose vessel, nominally a buoy tender, but with equipment and capabilities for ice breaking, search and rescue, fire fighting, logistics, oil spill response, and other tasks as well. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Hans Tiedge, top counter-spy of West Germany, defects to East Germany.
items.body: Hans-Joachim Tiedge was a head of West Germany's counter-intelligence in the Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV) in Cologne. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: British airship R-38 experiences structural failure over Hull in England and crashes in the Humber Estuary; of her 49 British and American training crew, only four survive.
items.body: The R.38 class of rigid airships was designed for Britain's Royal Navy during the final months of the First World War. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Western Roman army under Stilicho corners and defeats the Ostrogothic army in the battle of Faesulae.
items.body: In modern scholarship, the "late" period of the Roman army begins with the accession of the Emperor Diocletian in AD 284, and ends in 480 with the death of Julius Nepos, being roughly coterminous with the Dominate. One of those things you can't un-know.
